prompt.en: Listen: 'One small stick will snap in two, / Tie ten together, strong and ___!' Which word fits: 'true' or 'tight'?
prompt.hi: Suno: 'One small stick will snap in two, / Tie ten together, strong and ___!' Kaunsa word fit hoga, 'true' ya 'tight'? Rhyme ka dhyaan rakho.

challenges.hint: The missing word must rhyme with 'two'.

prompt.en: 'two' and 'true' are spelt differently at the end. Say them aloud. Do they rhyme?
prompt.hi: 'two' aur 'true' ki spelling alag hai. Dono ko zor se bolo. Kya rhyme karte hain?

challenges.hint: Rhyme is about sound, not letters.

prompt.en: The poem says, 'Together we can open doors.' Is it only about real doors? What does it mean?
prompt.hi: Poem kehti hai, 'Together we can open doors.' Kya sirf ghar ke darwaze ki baat hai? Iska matlab kya hai?

challenges.hint: A door can be a way into something new.

prompt.en: For the school exhibition, Aarav drew diagrams while Sana wrote labels. They finished a display neither could have completed in time alone. Which message fits better: “Sharing tasks helps a team” or “Drawing matters more than writing”?
prompt.hi: School exhibition ke liye Aarav ne diagrams banaye aur Sana ne labels likhe. Dono ne milkar display time par poora kiya. Kaunsa message better hai: “Sharing tasks helps a team” ya “Drawing matters more than writing”?

challenges.hint: Think about how dividing the work changed the result.

prompt.en: At a village sports day, Ravi tied a bell to the finish-line rope. The wind blew, the bell rang, and the runners looked up. Which happened second: tying the bell, the wind blowing, or the runners looking up?
prompt.hi: Gaon ke sports day par Ravi ne finish-line ki rassi par ghanti baandhi. Hawa chali, ghanti baji, aur runners ne upar dekha. Doosra kya hua: ghanti baandhna, hawa chalna, ya runners ka upar dekhna?

challenges.hint: Follow the events in the order given.

prompt.en: A notice near a metro station says: 'Cross only at the marked crossing. Wait until vehicles stop.' What is its main message: cross carefully at the marked place, or cross wherever there is space?
prompt.hi: Metro station ke paas notice hai: 'Sirf marked crossing par road paar karo. Gaadiyon ke rukne ka wait karo.' Iska main message kya hai: marked jagah par dhyan se cross karo, ya jahan jagah mile wahan cross karo?

challenges.hint: Find the message that includes the notice’s crossing rule.

options.text: cross carefully at the marked place

challenges.keyText: cross carefully at the marked place

prompt.en: Listen: 'When I read, I read my book, / I do not stop to stand and ___.' Which word fits: 'look' or 'see'?
prompt.hi: Suno: 'When I read, I read my book, / I do not stop to stand and ___.' 'look' ya 'see'? Rhyme socho.

challenges.hint: The missing word rhymes with 'book'.

prompt.en: Say 'care' and 'there'. The spellings are different. Do they rhyme?
prompt.hi: 'care' aur 'there' bolo. Spelling alag hai. Kya rhyme karte hain?

challenges.hint: Both end with an 'air' sound.

prompt.en: 'Zest' means: (a) great energy and joy (b) being sleepy (c) a kind of fruit. Which one?
prompt.hi: 'Zest' ka matlab: (a) bahut josh aur khushi (b) neend aana (c) ek fruit. Kaunsa?

challenges.hint: Is it fast and lively, or slow and sleepy?

options.text: (c) a kind of fruit. Which one

prompt.en: During a school trek, Riya shared her water with an injured classmate. The next day, that classmate helped Riya carry her bag. What lesson does this show: kindness can lead to friendship, or only strong people should help?
prompt.hi: School trek mein Riya ne injured classmate ko apna paani diya. Agle din us classmate ne Riya ka bag uthane mein help ki. Kya lesson milta hai: kindness se friendship badh sakti hai, ya sirf strong logon ko help karni chahiye?

challenges.hint: Notice that help went both ways.

prompt.en: How old was Louis when he hurt his eye?
prompt.hi: Louis ki aankh mein chot lagi tab woh kitne saal ka tha?

challenges.hint: It was in his father's workshop.

prompt.en: How many dots does the Braille system use?
prompt.hi: Braille system mein kitne dots hote hain?

challenges.hint: Louis made it simpler.

prompt.en: Louis 'invented' Braille. Is that the same as 'discovered'? Explain the difference.
prompt.hi: Louis ne Braille 'invent' kiya. Kya ye 'discover' jaisa hi hai? Farak samjhao.

challenges.hint: One word means make, the other means find.

prompt.en: At what time does the child in the poem get up?
prompt.hi: Poem mein bachcha kitne baje uthta hai?

challenges.hint: 'Up at ...'

prompt.en: The child says, 'That's why I'm always full of beans!' Does it mean the child ate many beans? What does it mean?
prompt.hi: Bachcha kehta hai, 'That's why I'm always full of beans!' Kya matlab usne bahut beans khaaye? Asal matlab kya hai?

challenges.hint: How does good food make you feel?

prompt.en: A boy sleeps late, eats chips and never plays. Will he feel 'full of beans'? Why?
prompt.hi: Ek ladka der se sota hai, chips khaata hai aur kabhi khelta nahi. Kya woh 'full of beans' feel karega? Kyun?

challenges.hint: Does the boy do those things?

prompt.en: After the morning kabaddi match, Aditi still wants to run another lap. Her coach says, “You’re full of beans!” Does the coach mean Aditi is energetic or hungry?
prompt.hi: Morning kabaddi match ke baad bhi Aditi ek aur lap daudna chahti hai. Coach kehte hain, “You’re full of beans!” Coach ka matlab energetic hai ya hungry?

challenges.hint: Think about what the coach notices after the match.

prompt.en: Rohan eats a bowl of beans at lunch but feels too tired to join cricket. His friend says, “Rohan is full of beans.” Is the saying used correctly? Answer yes or no, and say why.
prompt.hi: Rohan lunch mein ek bowl beans khata hai, par cricket khelne ke liye bahut thaka hai. Uska dost kehta hai, “Rohan is full of beans.” Kya saying sahi use hui hai? Yes ya no, aur kyun?

challenges.hint: Compare the saying’s meaning with Rohan’s condition.

prompt.en: What is a 'pile' of stones? (a) stones put one on top of another (b) stones thrown in a river (c) one big stone.
prompt.hi: Pathharon ka 'pile' kya hota hai? (a) ek ke upar ek rakhe pathhar (b) nadi mein phenke pathhar (c) ek bada pathhar.

challenges.hint: They are kept one on another.

options.text: (a) stones put one on top of another

challenges.keyText: (a) stones put one on top of another

prompt.en: During a school game, the cones fall. A player puts them back in their places. Which word best describes this action: aim, rebuild, or oppose?
prompt.hi: School game mein cones gir jaate hain. Ek player unhein wapas apni jagah rakhta hai. Is action ke liye kaunsa word sahi hai: aim, rebuild, ya oppose?

challenges.hint: Look for the word meaning ‘put back together’.

prompt.en: During lagori, Aarav throws the ball towards the stone pile, but it lands far to the left. His teammate says, “Adjust your aim.” What should Aarav change: where he throws or how fast he runs?
prompt.hi: Lagori mein Aarav ball stone pile ki taraf phenakta hai, par ball kaafi left mein girti hai. Teammate kehta hai, “Adjust your aim.” Aarav ko kya badalna chahiye: ball kahan phenke ya kitni tez daude?

challenges.hint: Think about what aim controls during a throw.

prompt.en: During a kho-kho match, Kabir held the rope firmly so it would not slip from his hands. In this sentence, does “firmly” mean securely or quickly?
prompt.hi: Kho-kho match ke dauraan Kabir ne rope firmly pakdi, taaki woh haathon se na phisle. Is sentence mein “firmly” ka matlab securely hai ya quickly?

challenges.hint: Use the reason after “so” to work out the meaning.

prompt.en: Can a swing really go higher than birds fly? Why does the poet say it?
prompt.hi: Kya jhoola sach mein chidiyon se upar ja sakta hai? Kavi aisa kyun kehta hai?

challenges.hint: Poems sometimes say things bigger than they are.

prompt.en: A banner beside the school swing moves gently back and forth in the breeze. Which sentence fits: 'The banner swayed' or 'The banner raced'?
prompt.hi: School swing ke paas ek banner hawa mein dheere se back and forth hilta hai. Kaunsa sentence fit hai: 'The banner swayed' ya 'The banner raced'?

challenges.hint: Choose the verb for gentle back-and-forth movement.

prompt.en: The pine trees 'stood in rows like green soldiers'. Were there real soldiers? What is the same?
prompt.hi: Pine ke ped 'stood in rows like green soldiers'. Kya wahan asli sainik the? Kya same hai?

challenges.hint: How did the pine trees stand?

prompt.en: What are 'ghats'? (a) wide steps going down into a river (b) a kind of boat (c) a saree.
prompt.hi: 'ghats' kya hote hain? (a) nadi mein utarti chaudi seedhiyan (b) ek tarah ki naav (c) ek saree.

challenges.hint: People bathe and pray there.

options.text: (a) wide steps going down into a river

challenges.keyText: (a) wide steps going down into a river

prompt.en: 'On the bank of the river Narmada.' Is this a money bank? How do you know?
prompt.hi: 'On the bank of the river Narmada.' Kya ye paise wala bank hai? Kaise pata?

challenges.hint: Is there money near a river?
